title: Yassa with Fish Balls and Prawns
localName: Yassa aux boulettes de poisson et crevettes
author: Aïssatou Mbaye
desc: Fish balls and prawns in an onion yassa, with a beugeudj of bissap leaves and okra pounded with lemon on the side.
longDesc: The most elaborate of her yassas and the only one with a sauce on the side. A seasoning farce of four garlic cloves, pepper and half a roughly cut bell pepper is pounded and reserved. Parsley, a vegetarian chilli, two more garlic cloves and a little salt are chopped, part of the farce is spread on the prawns, the fish flesh is added and mixed, and the mixture is formed into balls. The onion sauce takes the remaining farce with lemon juice and twenty centilitres of water, cooked about fifteen minutes on low heat, with the prawns and balls added at the end. The beugeudj is bissap leaves and okra cooked fifteen minutes in lightly salted water, drained, then pounded with salt and the juice of half a lemon.
ingredients: // Quantities printed only inside the steps
2 cloves garlic, for the fish mixture
The juice of 1 lemon, or 2 depending on size, for the sauce
// Sauce salt is given only as 'not too much'
equipment: Mortar and pestle, or a blender
steps: Pound 4 garlic cloves, pepper and half the roughly cut bell pepper into a seasoning farce. Reserve it.
Chop the parsley, the vegetarian chilli, 2 garlic cloves and a little salt together.
Spread part of the farce on the prawns, add the fish flesh, and mix.
// The source's cooking instruction for the balls is misprinted; see the note.
Soften the onions in hot oil with a chilli.
Once the onions turn translucent, add the remaining farce, a little salt — not too much — pepper, the lemon juice and 20 cl of water.
Cook about 15 minutes on low heat.
Add the prawns and the fish balls at the end.
Cook the bissap leaves and okra 15 minutes in lightly salted water, then drain.
Pound or blend them with salt and the juice of 1/2 a lemon.
Serve the yassa with the beugeudj alongside.
chefTips: The beugeudj on the side is what makes this version worth the extra work — a sharp, green, slightly slippery sauce against the sweet onions.
Not too much salt in the sauce, by her own instruction. The prawns and the fish balls are already seasoned with the farce.
Split the farce: part onto the prawns and into the fish mixture, the rest into the onion sauce. Same divided-seasoning logic as all her yassas.
Prawns and balls in at the very end only. They need minutes, not the fifteen the sauce takes.
Fifteen minutes in lightly salted water for the bissap leaves and okra, then pound. Do not skip the draining or the beugeudj will be watery.

Be aware the source's instruction for cooking the fish balls is misprinted — it reads as a temperature with the time unit missing, so no cooking time for the balls can be stated. Cook them through by eye.
Her line on the dish: it is a whole art, a whole alchemy between the ingredients and the flavours. For this one, which has three separate preparations, that is fair.
commonMistakes: Adding the prawns with the sauce rather than at the end.
Putting all the farce into the fish mixture.
Reading the misprinted ball-cooking instruction as minutes.
sources: Adapted from 'Yassa aux boulettes de poisson et crevettes', aistoucuisine.com, path /publications/yassa-aux-boulettes-de-poisson-et-crevettes. BYLINE: Aïssatou Mbaye. Date as printed: 29 juillet 2020. Yield: NONE PRINTED. Figures TWO-PASS. The Wolof name 'beugeudj' is used on the page for the bissap-leaf sauce.

A STRUCTURAL ABSENCE: NO INGREDIENT LIST reaches the page's HTML. Step-level quantities, with both passes agreeing: '4 gousses d'ail' in step 2; 'la moitié du poivron' in step 2; '2 gousses d'ail' in step 3; '20 cl d'eau' in step 7; '1/2 citron' in step 10; 'le jus d'un citron ou deux citrons selon la taille' in step 7; and 'un peu de sel' in step 3. NAMED WITHOUT QUANTITY: poivre, persil, piment végétarien, chair de poisson, crevettes, oignons, huile, feuilles de bissap, gombo. The sauce salt is given only as 'pas trop' — not too much. Step 1 is missing from the fetched text. The five servings above is editorial.

A MISPRINT IN THE SOURCE, flagged and NOT resolved: step 5 as printed reads 'cuire pendant 15 à 200 °C' — THE TIME UNIT IS MISSING. This is SINGLE-PASS, surfaced only by the structural pass. It is NOT assumed to mean minutes, and no cooking time or temperature for the fish balls is stated in this entry as a result. The step above says only to cook them through.

DONENESS CUES as printed in French: 'lorsque l'huile est un peu chaude' — when the oil is somewhat hot; 'lorsque les oignons deviennent translucides' — when the onions turn translucent; and 'Bien surveiller la cuisson des oignons' — watch the onion cooking closely.

THE BEUGEUDJ as printed: cook bissap leaves and okra 15 minutes in lightly salted water, drain, then pound or blend with salt and the juice of 1/2 a lemon. NOTE that this is the same preparation the MAGGI white-ceebu-jen printing at SEN005 spells 'béguète', and which Aïssatou Mbaye spells 'beuguedj' at SEN004. THREE SPELLINGS of one sauce across three pages, all recorded.
HER REMARK, quoted: 'C'est tout un art, toute une alchimie entre les aliments et les saveurs.'

A RETRIEVAL NOTE: the site is JavaScript-rendered, its ingredient lists were systematically unreachable, and step 1 was consistently missing. The figures came from a structured data-extraction pass rather than verbatim transcription.
reheating: Warm the sauce; add the prawns and balls back at the end.
healthBenefits: Fish and prawns together are very high in protein and low in saturated fat.
Bissap leaves supply vitamin C, calcium and iron.
culturalNote: Fish balls are a Saint-Louis and coastal habit — a way of stretching fish and using the pieces that will not steak cleanly — and pairing them with a sour green bissap-leaf sauce is the sort of combination that only comes from a place where both are to hand and nothing is wasted.
